data.text: The evidence is consistent and points to a single root cause. Let me record my findings.

data.cause: The vtnet0 WAN NIC driver transmit queue has hung (repeated watchdog timeouts), blocking all outbound traffic despite a valid lease and an operational cable modem; the allowed wan_reload renews DHCP but does not reset the wedged driver, which is why four reloads this outage did nothing and the watchdog hit its cap.
evidence: dmesg -a shows repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' interleaved with 'link state changed to DOWN/UP' cycles
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 and ping -c 3 -n 1.1.1.1 both fail with 'ping: sendto: No buffer space available' (ENOBUFS), 100% loss — output queue stuck
arp -a -n shows the directly-connected next hop 198.51.100.1 as '(incomplete)' while LAN neighbours resolve fine — ARP itself is not completing on the WAN NIC

ifconfig vtnet0: status active, correct leased address 198.51.100.27/24; netstat -rn shows default via 198.51.100.1 present; /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0 holds a valid lease (renew 2026/3/5) — so config/routing/DHCP are healthy

/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl and state.json: outage since ~02:01, watchdog issued 4 wan reloads during this outage (all rc=0) and hit its cap (reloads_24h 12/12, decision 'none' reason 'reload_cap') yet internet stayed down — a soft WAN reload cannot clear the wedged NIC

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl + modem-metrics.jsonl: modem 'registration complete', cm_status OPERATIONAL, uptime climbing, min_snr ~37.7dB — provider/CPE side is up, so the fault is on the firewall, not the ISP
ping -c 3 -n 10.20.0.9 succeeds with 0% loss and LAN ARP entry resolves — local services/LAN work, isolating the fault to the WAN NIC path
data.recommendation: A full reboot of gw.lan (firewall_reboot) is needed to reset the vtnet0 driver/NIC, since repeated wan_reload calls already proved ineffective against a hardware/driver-level hang. The maintainer is away tonight; request the reboot anyway and let the harness decide. After it recovers, investigate the recurring vtnet0 watchdog timeouts (driver/firmware) if they recur.
data.detail: vtnet0 WAN NIC transmit path wedged (watchdog timeouts)
